subject: medical-laboratory-science
intro: Medical laboratory science leads to the hidden half of medicine — the scientists and technologists whose tests diagnose disease, crossmatch blood and track infections from behind the lab door.

roles.title: Medical and Clinical Laboratory Technologists
roles.what: Perform complex medical laboratory tests for the diagnosis, treatment and prevention of disease — running the analysers and molecular platforms of haematology, chemistry, microbiology and blood banking, and training or supervising staff.
roles.where: Units 2 to 7 are the bench rotations: full blood counts, metabolic panels, culture and identification, crossmatching, serology and PCR. Unit 1's quality control and lab maths and unit 8's accreditation are the professional frame.

roles.title: Medical and Clinical Laboratory Technicians
roles.what: Perform routine medical laboratory tests for the diagnosis, treatment and prevention of disease, often under the supervision of a medical technologist — preparing specimens, running standard assays and recording results.
roles.where: Unit 1's specimen collection, handling and biosafety are the entry craft; urinalysis from unit 7 and routine chemistry and haematology panels from units 2 and 3 are the daily workload technicians own.

roles.title: Phlebotomists
roles.what: Draw blood for tests, transfusions, donations or research — explaining procedures to patients, keeping every collection safe and clean, and assisting patients who have adverse reactions to the draw.
roles.where: Unit 1 is the direct match: specimen collection and handling, biosafety and lab maths, plus the quality-control mindset that keeps a blood sample valid from vein to analyser.

roles.title: Physicians, Pathologists
roles.what: Diagnose disease and conduct laboratory tests using organs, body tissues and fluids — reading biopsies and cytology, directing the laboratory, and in forensic work serving as medical examiners.
roles.where: Units 2 to 6 give the disease science pathologists interpret — anaemias and leukaemias, culture and susceptibility, transfusion reactions and autoimmune serology; unit 7's molecular diagnostics is the growing edge of the specialty.
